transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Samir (Novapay Head of ML), Aisha (Platform Eng), Daniel (CTO), Priya (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Reviewed recent throughput runs, saw improvements with continuous batching but p99 spikes remain at high concurrency, looked at queueing behavior and batch sizes, agreed on next steps to increase concurrency test and run prod load window.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're on for 45 minutes, quick agenda  

- run through last week's bench, continuous batching updates, queueing knobs, and next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Samir: yeah that works, and just to flag, Daniel's got a meeting at 10:35 so we'll need the quick summary before then.
[00:25] Maya: perfect, we'll do a short recap at 10:30.
[00:30] Liam: ok jumping in 

- quick baseline numbers: last run we saw throughput at 560 tokens/sec on the v3 quantized model with continuous batching enabled, average latency around 160ms, but p99 hit 900ms under 120 concurrent users.
[00:48] Aisha: yeah those p99 spikes are the issue for us; our SLAs are 500ms p99 on API responses. we can tolerate occasional higher, but not sustained.
[01:05] Liam: right 

- so two things: queueing and effective batch timeout. With continuous batching the runtime will hold requests for a short window to build larger batches which increases throughput but can cause tail latency if there is a sudden burst and the queue gets saturated.
[01:27] Samir: can you remind me what our current queue_size and max_batch_latency are set to? I think we used defaults from the doc.
[01:33] Liam: current config on your POC cluster is queue_size=256 and max_batch_latency=12ms, and the scheduler will flush either when full or at that latency. For mixed prompt lengths that was a reasonable default but with your workload (many short prompts) we might reduce queue_size to 128 and reduce latency to 6-8ms to keep tails lower.
[01:55] Priya: if we reduce queue_size, won't throughput drop? we've got cost targets.
[02:03] Liam: yes slightly 

- throughput will go down but p99 will improve. It's a tradeoff. We measured about a 6-8% throughput drop when going from queue_size 256->128 but p99 improved by ~35% in our internal runs.
[02:20] Maya: and cost implications 

- less effective batching means more per-token cost, we should quantify that in the benchmark sheet.
[02:28] Samir: what's the concurrency target we should be testing? our production expected concurrency is more like 150 concurrent requests at peak. right now our POC runs used 120, which matched previous notes.
[02:39] Liam: for the next test we propose a 20% concurrency increase to 144 to see how the system behaves near your expected peak and exercise queueing. If that looks ok we can push to 200 to test headroom.
[02:52] Daniel: I'd also like to test a fallback path 

- if latency exceeds an SLO we want automatic fallback to a smaller model with similar semantics. is that possible in the POC?
[03:02] Maya: yes, we can configure smart routing with a fallback policy 

- Canary to smaller quantized variant 

- we've got that implemented in the POC, Liam can show details.
[03:12] Liam: yeah, we have a route policy that evaluates p95/p99; if average p99 crosses the threshold for two minutes, it will route new requests to the smaller model variant. There's a slight quality delta but it keeps your app responsive.
[03:30] Samir: ok good. One other thing 

- we saw occasional CUDA context preemption logs in the pod. do you think that's causing spikes?
[03:40] Liam: maybe 

- we saw some kernels stall when sequence lengths spiked. We can mitigate with pre-warming and by pinning the pod to GPUs (nodeAffinity) in Dedicated. For hosted it's trickier.
[03:51] Aisha: that brings up dedicated vs hosted 

- we need predictable latency, so Dedicated is attractive but cost is a concern. we want to measure what Dedicated would give us vs hosted with these queue settings.
[04:03] Maya: agreed 

- we can produce a Dedicated estimate with measured throughput numbers and expected unit cost. We'll include quantized vs unquantized runs.
[04:10] Samir: can you walk through the specific continuous-batching metrics we should look at in the logs?
[04:16] Liam: yes 

- key ones: batch_size distribution, wait_time_before_flush, KV cache hit ratio (for prefix caching), GPU_utilization, kernel_latency percentiles, and queue_depth histogram. We'll share a sheet with the relevant columns.
[04:34] Priya: on KV cache 

- are we seeing prefix cache usefulness? our workload has repeated prefixes for auth checks.
[04:40] Liam: early numbers show about 18% KV cache hit ratio, which helped average latency but didn't help the high tail. We can improve hit ratio by increasing session sharding affinity, but that's a config change.
[04:50] Maya: quick note 

- we've uploaded the benchmark sheet to the shared folder: https://redwood.com/benchmarks/novapay-poc (link in notes).
[05:00] Samir: yep saw it, thanks.
[05:12] Maya: ok let's look at the recent run details 

- Liam?
[05:18] Liam: sure 

- run at 120 concurrency, queue_size 256, max_batch_latency 12ms: throughput 560 tok/s, avg 160ms, p95 420ms, p99 900ms. run with queue_size 128, latency 8ms: throughput 520 tok/s, avg 170ms, p95 280ms, p99 580ms. run with continuous-batching disabled: throughput 320 tok/s, avg 240ms, p99 1.2s.
[05:48] Aisha: those numbers make sense 

- disabling continuous batching kills throughput. For us, the 128/8ms config looks promising since p99 below 600ms.
[05:58] Samir: can we get p99 down under 500ms? that's our goal.
[06:03] Liam: maybe 

- with queue tuning plus a small reduction in max sequence length (we can truncate long prompts) and slightly higher GPU memory to avoid preemption, we can push p99 under 500ms at 144 concurrency. Might be close.
[06:19] Daniel: is there room to change model quantization profile? we used int8 quantization v3 which is fast but sometimes increases kernel variance.
[06:29] Liam: we can try an alternative quant profile (mixed int8/4) or per-layer quantization. That might smooth p99 but could cost more memory or reduce throughput a bit. We'll have a tuning matrix.
[06:41] Maya: goal for next run: queue_size 128, max_batch_latency 8ms, concurrency 144, pre-warm pods, run for 30 minutes and capture full logs. Samir you ok to run that?
[06:53] Samir: yes we can run it this afternoon. I'll coordinate with Priya for pre-warm.
[06:59] Priya: yes 

- we'll pre-warm by sending ramp traffic for 5 minutes. we'll also disable node autoscaler during the test to keep pod placement stable.
[07:08] Liam: good call 

- autoscaler can cause cold starts that muddle numbers. Also set GPU affinity and disable preemption if possible for the test window.
[07:17] Maya: noted. We'll also enable verbose kernel tracing for two minutes at the start of the run to catch stalls.
[07:25] Samir: cool. On the fallback policy 

- can we get a failover response that returns a downgraded model but with a header indicating model-id so the app can degrade gracefully?
[07:35] Liam: yes 

- we support returning model metadata in headers, and the client can log that for A/B analysis. We'll include that in the route config.
[07:44] Aisha: operational question 

- how does queueing behave when we have token-limit long responses that occupy GPU longer?
[07:52] Liam: long responses will occupy the GPU and reduce effective batch throughput. We recommend separating long-generation routes from short-chat routes into different model endpoints or giving them a small dedicated pool. That way short requests aren't affected.
[08:06] Daniel: is that something we can try in the POC? route splitting?
[08:10] Maya: yes we can spin up a second route with smaller batch_size and dedicated pool for short responses. Probably small extra cost but big latency benefits.
[08:19] Samir: ok let's add that as an optional config for the next test.
[08:24] Maya: quick check 

- security and compliance questions? Any outstanding asks?
[08:27] Daniel: not on this call, we have the security deck and SOC2 report but will confirm EKM/KMS integration for private deploy later.
[08:35] Maya: cool 

- we'll follow up with the security pack link.
[08:40] Liam: another micro-optimization 

- leverage prefix/KV caching more aggressively by increasing session affinity TTL, for repeated auth prefixes we saw a measurable p95 benefit. That doesn't cost extra hardware.
[08:52] Aisha: how easy is it to change affinity?
[08:55] Liam: one flag in the routing config. We'll send the command.
[08:58] Samir: great.
[09:05] Maya: ok time check 

- Daniel needs to drop at 10:35 so quick recap in 2 minutes. Liam, any blockers from the SE side?
[09:12] Liam: none; we need the concurrency run results and logs. Also confirm if you'll keep autoscaler off during the in-prod load test on 12/08.
[09:21] Jules: Jules here 

- yes I will coordinate and get invites out for the 12/08 window and include Priya and Daniel.
[09:28] Daniel: thanks 

- I have to go now but this looks like a good plan.
[09:31] Daniel: (leaves)
[09:33] Maya: thanks Daniel, appreciate it.
[09:35] Samir: quick question 

- for dedicated pricing, can you give a rough delta against hosted per-token numbers?
[09:41] Maya: yes high level: Dedicated has higher fixed cost but lower marginal per-token after steady state. We'll share a sheet with modeled cost for your expected throughput.
[09:49] Samir: ok great.
[10:00] Aisha: one last thing 

- logging verbosity. We saw some noisy logs from the runtime level, can we filter to warnings by default?
[10:08] Liam: we can set log_level=info and filter debug events from kernel traces; for the test we'll enable verbose traces for a short window only.
[10:16] Priya: sounds good.
[10:20] Maya: recap and next steps: Samir to run concurrency 144 test this afternoon with pre-warm and autoscaler off; Maya to share benchmark sheet and logs link; Liam to send queueing tuning doc and recommended config; Jules to schedule 12/08 load window. We'll capture p95/p99 and share results.
[10:36] Samir: thanks everyone.
[10:38] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and confirm the 12/08 schedule. bye!

References/Artifacts referenced: https://redwood.com/benchmarks/novapay-poc (benchmark sheet), security deck link (https://redwood.com/security/novapay-pack), route config snippet (shared in chat), logs link (to be uploaded).
